message.content: I've reviewed the source; the DIF butterflies, twiddle-table folding, real-FFT reconstruction formulas, and DC/Nyquist special cases all check out mathematically. The main risk is runtime behavior (Triton gather, precision on extreme FP16 inputs, batch=256, storage offsets). I'll record a claim and run a comprehensive probe.

message.reasoning_content:
Let me analyze the kernel. Suspicious spots: _twiddle function. Phase range: phase = k * (256//width) for width up to M. For stage 0, width=M, phase up to (half-1)*(256/M)... Let's check _twiddle logic: cosine table is first quadrant of 256-point (65 entries, index 0..64). folded = min(phase, 128-phase); cosine = TABLE[folded], negated if phase>64. That handles phase in 0..128. But phase can be up to 128? For width=M, phase = (k & (M/2 -1)) * (256/M) ≤ (M/2-1)*(256/M) = 128 - 256/M < 128. OK. For the reconstruction twiddle: phase = k*(256/N), k up to M-1=N/2-1, phase up to (N/2-1)*(256/N) = 128 - 256/N. OK.

sine = TABLE[|64-phase|]. Hmm, sin(2π·phase/256) = cos(2π(phase-64)/256) = TABLE[|phase-64|]? For phase<64: cos(π/2 - x)=sin(x). |phase-64| = 64-phase, cos(2π(64-phase)/256) = cos(π/2 - 2π phase/256) = sin(2π phase/256). Yes correct for phase≤64. For phase>64: sin = cos(π/2 - θ)... for phase in (64,128], sin(2π phase/256) = cos(2π(phase-64)/256)... wait sin θ = cos(θ - π/2) = cos(2π(phase-64)/256), and |64-phase|=phase-64. Correct. So wi = -sine = -sin → e^{-iθ}. Fine.

Twiddle table accuracy: cosine table values are float64 exact enough.

The real-FFT reconstruction: standard. X[k] = 0.5*[ (Zr+Wr) + ... ]. Let me trust standard formula: Given Z = FFT of packed (x[2j]+i x[2j+1]), m = N/2. X[k] = 0.5*[(Zr[k]+Zr[M-k]) + cos(πk/M)(Zi[k]+Zi[M-k])... Standard: 
Xr[k] = 0.5*( (Zr[k]+Zr[M-k]) + (Zi[k]+Zi[M-k])*cosθ + (Zr[k]-Zr[M-k])*sinθ )
Wait signs. Known formula: with Z[k] = FFT_M(z),
X[k] = Re{ (Z[k] + conj(Z[M-k]))/2 + e^{-2πik/N} (Z[k] - conj(Z[M-k]))/2 }.
Z[k]-conj(Z[M-k]) = (Zr[k]-Zr[M-k]) + i(Zi[k]+Zi[M-k]).
e^{-iθ}*(a+ib) with a=Zr[k]-Zr[M-k], b=Zi[k]+Zi[M-k]: real = a cosθ + b sinθ, imag = b cosθ - a sinθ.
X[k] real = 0.5*[ (Zr[k]+Zr[M-k]) + a cosθ + b sinθ ].
Kernel: sr = ar+br (address = Z at k, partner = Z at -k mod M). di = ai + bi (Zi[k]+Zi[M-k]). dr = ar - br. xr = 0.5*(sr + wr*di + wi*dr) with wr=cos, wi=-sin → 0.5*(sr + cos*di - sin*dr). Correct.
xi = 0.5*(si - (wr*dr - wi*di)) = 0.5*(si - cos*dr - sin*di). Imag should be 0.5*[ (Zi[k]-Zi[M-k]) - a sinθ... imag = 0.5*[ b cosθ... wait imag part: X[k] imag = 0.5*[ (Zi[k]-Zi[M-k]) + (b cosθ - a sinθ) ]? Actually imag of sum: (Z[k]+conj Z[M-k])/2 imag = (Zi[k]-Zi[M-k])/2 = si/2. Imag of e^{-iθ}(a+ib) = b cosθ - a sinθ, halved. So xi = 0.5*(si + wr*dr... hmm imag of e^{-iθ}(a+ib) where e^{-iθ}=cos-i sin: (cos-i sin)(a+ib) = (ac + bs) + i(bc - as). Kernel: xi = 0.5*(si - (wr*dr - wi*di)) = 0.5*(si - cos*dr + wi... wi=-sin, so + wi*di = -sin*di... - (cos*dr - (-sin)di) = -cos*dr - sin*di. Hmm expected imag: si/2 + 0.5*(b cosθ - a sinθ) where a=dr, b=di. Kernel gives 0.5*(si - cos*dr - sin*di). That's 0.5*si - 0.5*cos*dr - 0.5*sin*di. Expected: 0.5*si + 0.5*cos*di - 0.5*sin*dr. Kernel's b cosθ term is -sin*di instead of +cos*di, and -cos*dr instead of -sin*dr. Wait that looks wrong! Unless my expansion is off.

Recompute: e^{-2πik/N} = cosθ - i sinθ. Multiply by (a + i b): (c - i s)(a+ib) = ac + i bc - i as + s b = (ac + sb) + i(bc - as). So real = ac + sb, imag = bc - as.

xr = 0.5*(sr + ac + sb) where kernel: wr*di + wi*dr = cos*di + wi*dr, wi = -sine... wait _twiddle returns (cosine, -sine). So wr=cos, wi=-sin. wr*di + wi*dr = cos*b - sin*a. Expected ac + sb = cos*a + sin*b. Kernel has cos*b - sin*a. That's wrong?? Hmm.

Hmm wait, maybe w in kernel is e^{+iθ}? wi=-sin means e^{-iθ} with (wr, wi). wr*di + wi*dr = b cos - a sin. Expected a cos + b sin. These differ. Let me double check the standard formula for real FFT.

X[k] = sum_{j=0}^{N-1} x[j] e^{-2πijk/N}. Split even/odd: E[k] + e^{-2πik/N} O[k] where E = FFT_{N/2}(x even), O = FFT_{N/2}(x odd), with k taken mod N/2. Packed z[j] = x[2j] + i x[2j+1], Z = FFT_M(z). Then E[k] = (Z[k] + conj(Z[M-k]))/2, O[k] = (Z[k] - conj(Z[M-k]))/(2i). X[k] = E[k] + e^{-2πik/N} O[k] = (Z[k]+conj Z[M-k])/2 + e^{-2πik/N}·(Z[k]-conj Z[M-k])/(2i).

1/i = -i, so e^{-iθ}/i... e^{-iθ}(-i) = -i cos - sin·... (-i)(c - is) = -ic - s = -s - ic. So X[k] = 0.5[(Z[k]+conjZ[M-k]) + (-s - ic)(Z[k]-conjZ[M-k])].

Z[k]-conjZ[M-k] = a+ib (a=Zr[k]-Zr[M-k], b=Zi[k]+Zi[M-k]). (-s - ic)(a+ib) = -sa - ib s - ica + c b = (cb - sa) + i(cb... compute carefully: (-s)(a) = -sa; (-s)(ib) = -isb; (-ic)(a) = -iac; (-ic)(ib) = cb. Total: (cb - sa) + i(cb... imaginary parts: -sb - ca. So imag = -(sb + ca).

Real: 0.5*(sr + cb - sa). Kernel: xr = 0.5*(sr + wr*di + wi*dr) = 0.5*(sr + c*b - s*a). ✓ matches (di=b, dr=a).
Imag: si = ai - bi = Zi[k]-Zi[M-k]. Imag expected: 0.5*(si - (sb + ca)) = 0.5*(si - s*b - c*a). Kernel: xi = 0.5*(si - (wr*dr - wi*di)) = 0.5*(si - (c*a - (-s)*b)) = 0.5*(si - c*a - s*b). ✓ matches. 

So formulas correct. Also Nyquist: X[M] = sum x[j](-1)^j = sum even - sum odd. E at k=M: Z[0]... X[M] = E[M] + e^{-iπ}O[M], E[M]=E[0]=(Zr[0]+Zr[0])/2... E[0] = Re(Z[0]), O[0] = Im(Z[0]). X[M] = Zr[0] - Zi[0] = ar - ai at k=0 where address=0, ar=Zr[0], ai=Zi[0]. ✓ matches line 83.

Also line 81-82 store for k in 0..M-1; k=M (Nyquist) via masked store. What about DC (k=0): xr = 0.5*(sr + c*di - s*dr) with θ=0: c=1, s=0 → 0.5*(ar+br+ai+bi) = 0.5*(Zr+Zr... at k=0, address=0, partner=0, so ar=br, ai=bi → xr = 0.5*(2ar + 2ai)?? wait di = ai + bi = 2ai. xr = 0.5*(2ar + 2ai) = ar + ai. Expected X[0] = sum x = sum even + sum odd = Zr[0] + Zi[0] = ar + ai. ✓. xi = 0.5*(si - dr) = 0.5*(ai - bi - (ar - br)) = 0. ✓.

So math looks right. Concerns: decimation-in-frequency loop. Stage loop: width = M>>stage, for DIF first stage should split k into first/second half of full array (width = M). half = M/2. left = k & ~half: for k < M/2, left=k, right=k (k&half=0 since half bit not set)? Hmm. For DIF: at first stage, butterfly pairs (k, k+half) for k<half. Kernel: left = k & ~half = k (for k<half, since half bit clear), right = k | half. For k ≥ half: left = k & ~half = k - half, right = k. Then lower = (k & half)==0 selects upper half: for k<half, real = a+b; for k≥half, real = d*wr - d... wait for k≥half, wr/wi computed from (k & (half-1)) which equals k-half. Good, that's DIF correctly: after all stages, output in bit-reversed order. ✓. And twiddle applied only to the subtracted half — DIF applies twiddles only in second half. ✓.

Also note gather left/right: for upper half (k≥half), left index = k-half, but values of real at that point are from previous stage — all fine since DIF uses in-place but distinct halves.

Potential issue: `tl.gather` axis=0 on 1D tensor — should work in Triton 3.4.

Precision: computes in float64, cos table float64 — should easily meet 1e-4 + 1e-6 tolerance since output rounded to fp32. Actually e^{-2πi} twiddles from table only approximate cos to ~1e-16. Fine.

Edge: N=64: m=32, LOG_M=4. 256//width: width=32 → 8. phase = (k&(15))*8 ≤ 112 <128 ok. Reconstruction phase = k*(256/64)=4k ≤ 124. ok.

Input storage offset: X pointer is values (contiguous), row*N offsets fine; nonzero storage offset — values tensor with storage_offset: Triton gets data_ptr including offset? Triton passes tensor, uses its data_ptr which includes storage offset. Actually triton uses tensor's data_ptr(), which accounts for storage offset. Fine. But validate_inputs requires is_contiguous — contiguous check is stride-based; a nonzero offset tensor can be contiguous. OK.

Batch 256: grid (batch,) fine. But note X row*N uses N (input width in elements); values is fp16, pointer arithmetic X + row*N correct since N columns.
